data.title: 3 ETFs That Could Deliver 14%+ Upside, According to the AI Analyst
data.description:

They help mitigate individual company-specific risk by providing exposure to a diversified portfolio of stocks. TipRanks' ETF Comparison Tool compares these 3 ETFs across key metrics:

Vanguard Growth ETF (VUG)

The VUG ETF tracks the Morningstar U.S. Large Cap Growth Index and includes leading growth stocks. It provides a diversified exposure to industry giants and innovative leaders known for a track record of delivering solid growth. The ETF AI Analyst has an average price target of $97 on the VUG ETF, implying about 18.1% upside potential. The Outperform rating on VUG reflects its notable exposure to prominent tech companies such as Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), and Alphabet (GOOGL).

Invesco NASDAQ 100 ETF (QQQM)

The QQQM ETF tracks the NASDAQ-100 (NDX) and provides exposure to the non-financial companies on the index. It is suitable for investors looking for exposure to leading companies in sectors such as technology, consumer goods, and healthcare. The ETF AI Analyst has an Outperform rating on the QQQM ETF with a price target of $317, implying 17.3% upside potential. The AI Analyst's bullish stance on QQQM is based on leading tech companies such as Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia (NVDA), and Alphabet.

iShares Core S&P Total U.S. Stock Market ETF (ITOT)

The ITOT ETF tracks the S&P Total Market Index and helps investors gain exposure to attractive stocks across all market caps. It helps to capitalize on the growth potential of companies across the full spectrum of the U.S. stock market, from small-cap innovators to established large-cap leaders. The ETF AI Analyst has an Outperform rating on the ITOT ETF with a price target of $184, implying 14.6% upside potential. The AI Analyst's bullish stance on ITOT is based on holdings such as Apple, Microsoft, and Alphabet.

data.title: Stock Market Wrap: S&P, Nasdaq Advanced on Encouraging Jobs Data as AI Stocks Rebounded
data.description:
Both the S&P 500 (SPX) and the Nasdaq 100 (NDX) closed higher on Friday, one day after the two indexes posted their worst single-day declines since April 2025. The S&P 500 ETF finished with a 0.31% gain, while the Nasdaq 100 ETF rose 1.35%.

News That Moved the Stock Market Today

  • In October, nonfarm payrolls increased by 165,000, well above expectations of 70,000. The professional and business services sector led the way with 70,000 additions, followed by healthcare with 42,000. Furthermore, August's payrolls were revised up to 186,000 from 133,000, while September's figure was raised to 60,000 from 29,000. The U.S. has added an average of 86,000 jobs per month this year, compared with just 10,000 in 2025.
  • The unemployment rate came in at 4.1%, down from 4.2% in September and below the estimate of 4.2%.
  • AI stocks rebounded from a steep selloff on Thursday caused by concerns that the Democrats' midterm victories could lead to stricter AI regulations and delays to data center construction. Nvidia (NVDA), AMD (AMD), and Intel (INTC) all closed in the green.
  • Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa alleviated some of those fears after she clarified that she doesn't oppose new data centers but wants companies to speak with local residents and address their concerns before building new facilities. Texas is home to nearly 30% of the data center capacity planned across the U.S. "It is not that I hate data centers," Hinojosa said. "I hate the way they are taking advantage of Texas and that stops when I'm governor."
  • The University of Michigan's preliminary Index of Consumer Sentiment rose to 51.0 in November from 48.0 in October, beating expectations of 48.0. Meanwhile, consumers' year-ahead inflation expectations eased to 4.3% from 4.7%, while long-term expectations edged down to 3.4% from 3.5%.
  • Microsoft (MSFT) said it will wind down the amount of computing capacity it rents from Oracle (ORCL) as it reviews its partnerships with cloud providers.
  • Deutsche Bank analyst Edison Yu reiterated his $250 price target for SpaceX (SPCX) and addressed concerns that Elon Musk's financial support for Republican candidates in the midterm elections could expose the company to political backlash. Yu noted that most of SpaceX's government business is with executive-branch agencies rather than Congress.
data.author: Eddie Pan

data.title: Why SpaceX Stock (SPCX) Jumped 8% Today – November 6, 2026
data.description:
Space and AI company SpaceX (SPCX) jumped by 8.6% in Friday's trading after CEO Elon Musk predicted on X that U.S. government contracts would account for less than 10% of fourth-quarter revenue, down from 16.6% in the third quarter. Musk also said at a Baron investment conference that revenue could grow by roughly 70% from the previous quarter and that its annualized revenue could exceed $500 billion by the end of 2027.

Interestingly, NASA and the Pentagon used to be SpaceX's most important customers, and government agencies still made up roughly 20% of its revenue in 2025. Musk now expects their share to fall below 5% within a year. However, that does not necessarily mean that government payments are declining. Revenue from other customers could simply be growing much faster.

This change is already visible in SpaceX's financial results. Third-quarter revenue increased by 161% from a year earlier to $14.6 billion. Its AI division generated $7.56 billion, compared with $5.25 billion from satellite connectivity services and $1.77 billion from space operations.

The AI division also reported $431 million in operating profit after losing $1.26 billion in the previous quarter.

Why SpaceX's AI Growth Brings New Risks

Musk's latest prediction means that fourth-quarter revenue could reach approximately $25 billion if sales grow by 70% as expected. That would put SpaceX near a $100 billion annual revenue pace. His $500 billion projection refers to a potential revenue pace at the end of 2027, rather than total revenue for that year. However, the company's growing AI business has created another risk. AI developer Anthropic accounted for 34.5% of SpaceX's third-quarter revenue, or roughly $5 billion.

That is more than twice the government's share. Furthermore, Anthropic's agreements allow either company to cancel after initial commitment periods that end in early 2027, provided that 90 days' notice is given. This means that SpaceX could lose a significant amount of revenue if Anthropic eventually switches to another provider.

Is SPCX Stock a Good Buy?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on SPCX stock based on 28 Buys, five Holds, and one Sell assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. Furthermore, the average SPCX price target of $253.57 per share implies 88.9% upside potential. (See SPCX Stock Forecast).

data.title: Google Takes Over Crusoe's Wyoming AI Project in $17 Billion Expansion
data.description:
Tech giant Google (GOOGL) has acquired AI infrastructure company Crusoe's planned computing facility in Wyoming after the startup struggled to secure customers. The takeover comes as Google plans to invest $17 billion in its first major computing campus in the state. However, the companies did not disclose the purchase price, so the $17 billion is Google's planned investment rather than what it paid Crusoe.

According to Bloomberg, Crusoe originally announced the project in July 2025 alongside energy infrastructure company Tallgrass. At the time, Crusoe said that the facility could eventually expand to 10 gigawatts of power capacity, which is enough to supply electricity to roughly 7.5 million homes. However, Google has not committed to building a facility that large.

The project ran into problems earlier this year after Crusoe struggled to secure customers, including Google. The tech giant reportedly questioned the project's costs and construction schedule, which eventually led to Crusoe being pushed aside.

Nevertheless, Crusoe confirmed on Friday that it had completed early work on the project. This included choosing the location and obtaining government approvals. It also helped plan how the facility would receive electricity.

How Google Plans to Power Its $17 Billion Project

Electricity is a major part of Google's investment because AI facilities require enormous amounts of power to operate. The Wyoming project will feature a planned 702-megawatt power system that uses natural gas fuel cells supplied by energy technology company Bloom Energy (BE). Utility provider American Electric Power (AEP) is also involved in the development.

Google plans to capture much of the carbon dioxide produced by the fuel cells and store it underground. The company also says that it will pay for all the electricity it uses and rely on air cooling to reduce water consumption. Google expects its Wyoming investment to generate hundreds of millions of dollars in local property taxes.

The expansion comes as Google's cloud business grows. Google Cloud revenue increased by 103% to $30.7 billion last quarter. Meanwhile, the firm expects to spend between $195 billion and $205 billion on capital projects in 2026.

Despite losing the Wyoming project, Crusoe still has more than six gigawatts of computing capacity under contract. It also has over 40 gigawatts of potential projects in development and is building another facility for Google in Texas.

Are GOOGL Shares a Good Buy?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on GOOGL stock based on 30 Buys and four Holds assigned in the past three months. Furthermore, the average GOOGL price target of $398.48 per share implies 40% upside potential. (See GOOGL Stock Forecast).
data.author: Vince Condarcuri

data.title: S&P 500 Top Stock Gainers Today, 11/6/26
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SPX) closed with a 0.31% return on Friday as AI stocks rebounded from a sharp pullback alongside an encouraging jobs report. Information technology led all sectors with a 1.26% gain, while consumer staples stocks lagged with a 1.21% loss.

Let's break down the sectors behind the performance.

Today's Top-Performing S&P 500 Sector 

Information technology was the top-performing sector after comments from Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa helped ease concerns about potential restrictions on data center construction. Hinojosa clarified that she doesn't oppose new data centers but instead wants AI companies to consult local residents before moving forward with new projects. This reassured investors given that Texas is home to nearly 30% of the data center capacity planned across the U.S. Meanwhile, Coherent (COHR) led the group higher after the photonics manufacturer posted third-quarter revenue growth of 50% to $2.37 billion, topping expectations of $2.31 billion.

Several information technology stocks led the sector's gains, including:

  • Coherent (COHR)
  • AMD (AMD)
  • Intel (INTC)
  • Lam Research (LRCX)
  • Akamai Technologies (AKAM)

Today's Worst-Performing S&P 500 Sector 

Meanwhile, the consumer staples sector faced the largest drawdown as investors rotated out of defensive stocks and into tech stocks following Thursday's selloff. Furthermore, consumer staples stocks had outperformed over the past five sessions, potentially prompting some investors to lock in gains. Monster Beverage (MNST) faced losses after the company posted third-quarter revenue growth of 16.7% to $2.56 billion and an adjusted EPS of 30 cents. Wall Street was expecting $2.5 billion and 30 cents, respectively.

Notable consumer staples stocks trading lower include:

  • McCormick & Company (MKC)
  • Dollar Tree (DLTR)
  • General Mills (GIS)
  • Hormel Foods (HRL)
  • Monster Beverage (MNST)

data.title: 3 Hidden 'Strong Buy' Data Center Stocks to Bet on as Development Risk Rises
data.description:
This week, data center stocks sold off after the Democrats won control of the U.S. Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections. The news sparked fears of bigger political pushback against the rapid development of data centers. Still, Wall Street analysts are bullish on three not-so-popular data center-related names: Dycom (DY), Fabrinet (FN), and Belden (BDC). Each stock has a Strong Buy consensus rating from Wall Street analysts, with at least 50% upside, according to TipRanks' Compare Top Data Center Stocks tool.

Dycom leads the group with about 161% upside based on the average price target of $545.50. These companies play key roles in the data center supply chain. Despite the risk, these companies remain tied to the AI infrastructure buildout.

Dycom (DY)

Dycom is an American specialty contracting services company. The Florida-based business provides electrical infrastructure to data centers.

Dycom also supports companies in the telecom and utility industries. Its engineering and construction services help these firms expand their infrastructure.

Dycom's shares are down 43% since the start of the year. However, analysts still see room for a 161% jump over the coming months. This is based on analysts' average price target of $545.50.

Fabrinet (FN)

Fabrinet is a contract manufacturing company based in the Cayman Islands. The firm produces optical packaging products, including high-speed optical transceivers and active fiber-optic cables. As AI applications expand, the need for rapid data transfer also grows. The industry considers optical-based systems a key solution.

Fabrinet counts Nvidia (NVDA) and Cisco (CSCO) as customers. The company's shares are down about 36% year-to-date. Still, analysts expect an 84% rally over the next 12 months. This is based on the average price target of $593.

Belden (BDC)

Belden is a U.S. communications equipment company based in Missouri. The firm designs, manufactures, and sells high-performance networking and connectivity products.

Its product lineup includes Ethernet, fiber-optic, and coaxial cables; server enclosures and racks; and industrial routers. The company also offers cybersecurity software.

Belden also offers services to install, run, and maintain these products. The company is behind brands such as cable makers Alpha Wire and Mohawk, as well as industrial networking solutions provider Hirschmann.

Belden's shares have fallen more than 17% since the start of the year. Yet analysts have forecast about 54% upside ahead. This is based on the average price target of $153.33.

data.title: Boeing Stock (NYSE:BA) Notches Up with CapeWeek Plans
data.description:
CapeWeek might be one of the biggest things to hit aerospace stock Boeing (BA) since the last strike, and the good news is that, this time, it is good news. CapeWeek is an event that NASA is planning to launch, and there is a good chance that Boeing will be front and center if it goes off. Boeing stock gained fractionally in Friday afternoon's trading. Boeing has also seen a 12.21% loss in its share price over the past year.

CapeWeek Bound

NASA is getting ready for a new show known as CapeWeek, which will start up at Florida's Kennedy Space Center in 2028. This is intended as a way to bring aerospace shows back to the United States, where previously London and Paris were the center of future aerospace launches. The Paris Air Show as well as the Farnborough event were both major venues for Boeing and rival Airbus (EADSY) to show off some of their upcoming developments. It is intended that CapeWeek will be the equivalent of that for the United States.

The idea that Boeing will show off its new plane at CapeWeek is not confirmed, of course, but is a distinct possibility. Certainly, considering the sheer amount of sales that the United States government has helped Boeing accomplish, as well as the current number of contracts Boeing has with the United States government, it would be worthwhile for Boeing to make an appearance and help get CapeWeek off the ground.

AI-Driven Inspector Drones

Boeing had a lot of trouble in the last few years with product quality, and rebuilt its entire corporate culture in a bid to get more credibility behind it, hoping to rebuild a damaged reputation. The latest development may not help with that as Boeing is currently undertaking drone inspections of some of its aircraft using an artificial intelligence program.

Reports note that Boeing's Advanced Aircraft Inspection program uses camera-equipped drones to circulate around the aircraft, taking pictures of the exterior. Then Boeing's Automated Damage Detection Software kicks in to check the photographs for possible damage, before sending the reports on to human technicians for review. Boeing points out that such a plan would likely shorten inspection time as well as keep live human employees off elevated platforms where the risk of falling is substantial.

Is Boeing a Good Stock to Buy Right Now?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on BA stock based on 18 Buys and one Hold assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. The average BA price target of $235.35 per share implies 36.01% upside potential.

data.title: Microsoft (MSFT) to Reduce the AI Compute It Rents from Oracle
data.description:
Media reports say that technology giant Microsoft (MSFT) plans to wind down the artificial intelligence (AI) computing capacity it rents from Oracle (ORCL). Microsoft has reportedly been turning off rented computing capacity from Oracle after declining to renew the contract.

The computing capacity had become less useful because it no longer met Microsoft's requirements. The Oracle servers used older-generation Nvidia (NVDA) microchips that struggled to handle Microsoft's AI computing needs. The agreement, announced in 2023, involved Oracle providing Microsoft access to servers that would power a new AI-assisted version of its Bing search engine.

Microsoft's key performance indicators. Source: TipRanks

Bad News for Oracle

The value of the deal between Microsoft and Oracle has not been made public, Regardless, the end of the arrangement will result in a loss of revenue for Oracle. Microsoft has also reportedly decided against expanding its computing agreement with British AI cloud provider Nscale at a Texas data center facility.

The potential extension would have been worth tens of billions of dollars to Nscale. Microsoft has been taking a more cautious approach to renting AI computing capacity from third-party providers amid concerns about project delays, regulatory hurdles, and rising costs. The company is also directing more spending toward expanding its own data center capacity.

Cost-Cutting at Microsoft

Microsoft has been looking to cut costs and achieve efficiencies wherever it can across its business. In recent weeks, the company announced that it has offered voluntary buyout packages to 60,000 of its employees as it moves to adopt more AI internally. The buyout packages have been offered to workers in the U.S., Canada, India, and the United Kingdom.

In April of this year, Microsoft announced its first-ever voluntary retirement program, which targeted about 7% of its U.S. employees. The latest buyout offer to employees also comes as Microsoft transforms its business model, trying to charge clients based on how much AI they use. The company is one of the few hyperscalers that has managed to maintain positive free cash flow despite heavy spending on AI.

Microsoft reported free cash flow of $18.63 billion for the latest quarter despite $45.2 billion worth of capital expenditures and finance leases related to AI infrastructure.

Is MSFT Stock a Buy?

Microsoft's stock has a consensus Strong Buy rating among 37 Wall Street analysts. That rating is based on 35 Buy and two Hold recommendations issued in the last three months. The average MSFT price target of $611.85 implies 15% upside from current levels.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: Why Is Penny Stock SunCar Technology Group (SDA) Up 132% Today?
data.description:
SunCar Technology Group (SDA) stock rocketed higher on Friday after the Chinese automotive company announced preliminary earnings and a share repurchase program. Starting with earnings, the company revealed unaudited revenue for the first nine months ending September 30, 2026 of approximately $426.4 million. This would mark a 25% increase when compared to its revenue from the same period of 2025.

SunCar Technology Group noted that its revenue growth was largely due to improvements across its various sectors. For example, unaudited Auto Services Revenue is expected to increase 22% year-over-year to $185.4 million. The company also expects its Auto eInsurance revenue to reach $197.4 million, which would be a 32% year-over-year increase. It also noted that Technology Services revenue for the period should increase 19% to $43.6 million.

"Looking ahead, the company will continue to capitalize on China's large automotive services market, its continuous path to full digitalization, and the rapidly expanding EV segment, actively pursuing new potential partners and capturing key new verticals," said SunCar Technology Group CFO Eric Zhang.

SDA Share Repurchase Plan

SunCar Technology Group also announced a share repurchase plan today. Its Board of Directors has approved the repurchase of $10 million worth of SDA stock. The company said that it will fund these purchases with cash on hand and cash from operations. These repurchases are set to take place from time to time over the next three months.

Investors reacting well to a share repurchase makes sense. They often improve investor morale and signal confidence from the company's leadership team.

SDA Stock Movement Today

SDA stock experienced a strong 131.92% rally on Friday. However, the shares were still down 92.43% year-to-date and have fallen 92.15% over the past 12 months.

With today's preliminary earnings and share repurchase news came heavy trading of SDA stock. This saw some 443 million shares change hands, compared to a three-month average daily trading volume of about 552,000 shares.

Is SunCar Technology Group Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Turning to Wall Street, the analysts' consensus rating for SunCar Technology Group is Moderate Buy, based on one Buy rating over the past three months. BTIG analyst Marvin Fong reiterated this rating on September 25, 2026. He also lowered his price target for the shares to $4 from $5, suggesting a possible 2,514.38% upside for the shares. (See SDA Stock Forecast)
